title: Negligence, damages and liability
summary: A slip at Tony's Pizza: the four elements of negligence, Michigan's comparative fault rule, the kinds of damages, and absolute, strict and vicarious liability.
objectives: Name the four elements of negligence and the main defenses
Apply Michigan's comparative fault rule to a damage award
Classify special, general and punitive damages
Tell absolute, strict and vicarious liability apart

scenes.subtitle: Negligence, Michigan's fault rules, the kinds of damages, and three special kinds of liability

scenes.title: Rosa slips: was Tony negligent?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: negligence; ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. I, Cov. A.1.a; memory hook mn_core-11; question core-024
scenes.plain: Not using the reasonable care you owe someone, and causing them real harm.
scenes.example: Tony saw the slush puddle and left it there for an hour: no mop, no sign. Rosa slipped on it and broke her leg.
scenes.exam: Intent to harm is NOT an element. On an EXCEPT question, intent is usually the odd one out.

beats.text: An hour later, Rosa hurries in, eyes on her phone, slips on the puddle and breaks her leg.
beats.say: An hour later, Rosa hurries in, eyes on her phone, slips on the puddle and breaks her leg.

beats.text: Ow! My leg!

beats.text: She sues Tony. In exam words, she's the plaintiff and Tony's the defendant.

scenes.title: What Rosa must prove
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: negligence; proximate cause; memory hook mn_core-11; question core-024

draw.text: I never meant to hurt anyone!

spots.label: Duty
spots.text: Rosa was a customer at Tony's Pizza. First, she must show that Tony owed her a legal duty of care.

spots.label: Breach
spots.text: Breach means failing to use the care that was reasonable. Rosa points to the puddle Tony saw and left for an hour: no mop, no sign.

spots.label: Proximate cause
spots.text: The breach set off a foreseeable chain of events: puddle, slip, broken leg. The breach led to the harm.

spots.label: Damage
spots.text: A broken leg is an actual injury. Without actual injury or damage, there's no negligence claim.

spots.label: Not an element: intent
spots.text: Tony never meant to hurt anyone. Intent to harm is not an element of negligence, so Rosa doesn't have to prove it.

beats.text: To win, Rosa must prove all four elements. The hook: Don't Break People's Doors. Duty, breach, proximate cause, damage.
beats.say: To win, Rosa must prove all four elements. The hook: Don't Break People's Doors. Duty, breach, proximate cause, damage.

beats.text: Tap each glowing spot.
beats.say: Tap each glowing spot.

reveal.text: She must show duty: Tony owed her a duty of care under the law. Breach: he didn't use reasonable care.
reveal.say: She must show duty: Tony owed her a duty of care under the law. Breach: he didn't use reasonable care.

reveal.text: Proximate cause: a foreseeable chain, puddle to slip to broken leg. Damage: an actual injury. No intent needed.
reveal.say: Proximate cause: a foreseeable chain, puddle to slip to broken leg. Damage: an actual injury. No intent needed.

scenes.title: What can Rosa ask for? Three kinds of damages
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: compensatory, special, general, punitive damages; Gilbert (Mich 2004), via IADC compendium; hook mn_core-13

draw.text: Compensatory: amends for the actual loss
Medical bills, lost wages, loss of use
Beyond compensation: for wanton or willful wrongdoing
Only if a statute expressly says so

beats.text: What can Rosa ask for? Compensatory damages make amends for her actual loss. They come in two types.
beats.say: What can Rosa ask for? Compensatory damages make amends for her actual loss. They come in two types.

beats.text: Special equals Spreadsheet: losses you can add up, like medical bills, lost wages and loss of use.
beats.say: Special equals Spreadsheet: losses you can add up, like medical bills, lost wages and loss of use.

beats.text: General equals Gut: a subjective award for pain and suffering.
beats.say: General equals Gut: a subjective award for pain and suffering.

beats.text: Punitive equals Punish: extra money beyond compensation, to punish particularly wanton or willful wrongdoing.
beats.say: Punitive equals Punish: extra money beyond compensation, to punish particularly wanton or willful wrongdoing.

beats.text: In Michigan, punish needs permission: punitive damages generally aren't recoverable unless the Legislature expressly authorizes them by statute.
beats.say: In Michigan, punish needs permission: punitive damages generally aren't recoverable unless the Legislature expressly authorizes them by statute.

scenes.title: Rosa's claim: where do the lost wages go?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: compensatory, special, general, punitive damages; Gilbert (Mich 2004), via IADC; questions core-bas-07, core-bas-08, core-027
scenes.ask: Where do her lost wages go?

beats.text: Rosa lists her losses: hospital bills, six weeks of lost wages, and the pain.
beats.say: Rosa lists her losses: hospital bills, six weeks of lost wages, and the pain.

beats.text: Tony was careless, not wanton or willful. Where do the lost wages go?
beats.say: Tony was careless, not wanton or willful. Where do the lost wages go?

options.label: List them as general damages

beats.text: General? No. Wages add up, like her bills: special. General is the subjective award for pain and suffering.
beats.say: General? No. Wages add up, like her bills: special. General is the subjective award for pain and suffering.

options.fail: Lost wages can be added up, so they are special damages. General damages are the subjective award for pain and suffering.

options.label: List them as special damages

beats.text: Lost wages add up, like her bills: special damages. Her pain and suffering is general. Both are compensatory.
beats.say: Lost wages add up, like her bills: special damages. Her pain and suffering is general. Both are compensatory.

options.win: Lost wages add up, like her medical bills: special damages. Pain and suffering is general. Both are compensatory.

options.label: As punitive damages: make Tony pay extra!

beats.text: Punish him! Make it huge!
beats.say: Punish him! Make it huge!

beats.text: Lost wages are an actual loss: compensatory. Punitive damages punish wanton or willful conduct, and Tony was only careless.
beats.say: Lost wages are an actual loss: compensatory. Punitive damages punish wanton or willful conduct, and Tony was only careless.

options.fail: Lost wages are compensatory. Punitive damages punish wanton or willful conduct; Tony was careless. In Michigan, they need express statutory authority.

reveal.text: Special plus general: both compensatory. Punitive damages go beyond compensation, to punish.
reveal.say: Special plus general: both compensatory. Punitive damages go beyond compensation, to punish.

scenes.title: Rosa was on her phone: three defenses
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: contributory, comparative negligence; assumption of risk; MCL 600.2958; MCL 600.2959; hook mn_core-12

draw.text: Damages cut by your % of fault

beats.text: But Rosa was on her phone. Can Tony pay less, or nothing? Three general defenses; Michigan's rule comes last.
beats.say: But Rosa was on her phone. Can Tony pay less, or nothing? Three general defenses; Michigan's rule comes last.

beats.text: Contributory negligence, the old common-law rule: any fault of yours, zero dollars. Many states have replaced it.
beats.say: Contributory negligence, the old common-law rule: any fault of yours, zero dollars. Many states have replaced it.

beats.text: Comparative negligence: your damages are reduced by your percentage of fault. You lose your percentage.
beats.say: Comparative negligence: your damages are reduced by your percentage of fault. You lose your percentage.

beats.text: Assumption of risk: if you knowingly and voluntarily accept a known risk, you can't recover for the resulting injury.
beats.say: Assumption of risk: if you knowingly and voluntarily accept a known risk, you can't recover for the resulting injury.

beats.text: In Michigan, a plaintiff's own fault doesn't bar recovery. It reduces her damages by her percentage of fault.
beats.say: In Michigan, a plaintiff's own fault doesn't bar recovery. It reduces her damages by her percentage of fault.

scenes.title: Tony's call: what does he argue?
scenes.src: MCL 600.2958; MCL 600.2959; IRMI glossary: contributory, comparative negligence; question core-026
scenes.ask: What does Tony argue she gets?

beats.text: Trial day. The jury finds Tony negligent and puts Rosa's economic damages at $100,000.
beats.say: Trial day. The jury finds Tony negligent and puts Rosa's economic damages at one hundred thousand dollars.

beats.text: But it also finds her 30% at fault. What does Tony argue she gets?
beats.say: But it also finds her thirty percent at fault. What does Tony argue she gets?

options.label: $0: any fault means she gets nothing!
options.fail: That's contributory negligence, the old common-law rule. In Michigan, a plaintiff's own fault doesn't bar recovery; it reduces her damages.

beats.text: She was on her phone! Zero!
beats.say: She was on her phone! Zero!

beats.text: The judge says no. That's the old contributory rule. In Michigan, her own fault doesn't bar recovery.
beats.say: The judge says no. That's the old contributory rule. In Michigan, her own fault doesn't bar recovery.

draw.text: She was on her phone! Zero!

options.label: $30,000: her 30% share

beats.text: $30,000? The judge says no: her damages are cut by her 30% share, not down to it.
beats.say: Thirty thousand dollars? The judge says no: her damages are cut by her thirty percent share, not down to it.

options.fail: Comparative fault reduces her damages by her 30% share: $100,000 minus $30,000 leaves $70,000. The $30,000 is the part she loses.

draw.text: Cut by 30%, not down to it

options.label: $70,000: not the full $100,000
options.win: In Michigan, damages are reduced by the plaintiff's percentage of fault: $100,000 of economic damages minus her 30% share leaves $70,000.

beats.text: The judge agrees. 30% of $100,000 is $30,000, so Rosa recovers $70,000 of her economic damages.
beats.say: The judge agrees. Thirty percent of one hundred thousand dollars is thirty thousand dollars, so Rosa recovers seventy thousand dollars of her economic damages.

reveal.text: Michigan's rule: your own fault doesn't bar you. It cuts your damages by your share.
reveal.say: Michigan's rule: your own fault doesn't bar you. It cuts your damages by your share.

scenes.title: Michigan's 50% line
scenes.src: MCL 600.2959; MCL 500.3135(2)(b); memory hook mn_core-12; question core-025
scenes.plain: Fault greater than everyone else's combined: economic damages still reduced, but no noneconomic damages.
scenes.example: Had the jury found Rosa 60% at fault: economic damages minus 60%, and nothing for pain and suffering.
scenes.exam: Michigan auto no-fault suits for noneconomic loss: a party over 50% at fault recovers nothing.

beats.text: Michigan draws one more line. If a plaintiff's fault is greater than everyone else's combined, so more than 50%, noneconomic damages, like pain and suffering, are not awarded. Her economic damages are still awarded, reduced by her percentage of fault.
beats.say: Michigan draws one more line. If a plaintiff's fault is greater than everyone else's combined, so more than fifty percent, noneconomic damages, like pain and suffering, are not awarded. Her economic damages are still awarded, reduced by her percentage of fault.

beats.text: Had the jury found Rosa 60% at fault and Tony 40%: economic damages minus 60%, and nothing for pain and suffering.
beats.say: Had the jury found Rosa sixty percent at fault and Tony forty percent: economic damages minus sixty percent, and nothing for pain and suffering.

beats.text: In Michigan, auto no-fault suits for noneconomic loss use a different rule: a party more than 50% at fault recovers nothing.
beats.say: In Michigan, auto no-fault suits for noneconomic loss use a different rule: a party more than fifty percent at fault recovers nothing.

scenes.q: Suppose the jury had found Rosa exactly 50% at fault in her Michigan negligence suit. What happens to her noneconomic damages, like pain and suffering?
scenes.why: Michigan cuts off noneconomic damages only when the plaintiff's fault is more than 50%. At exactly 50%, they are reduced by her share.

beats.text: Here's a trap. Say the jury had found Rosa exactly 50% at fault. What happens to her pain and suffering damages?
beats.say: Here's a trap. Say the jury had found Rosa exactly fifty percent at fault. What happens to her pain and suffering damages?

reveal.text: Reduced by 50%, not barred. The cutoff applies only above 50%, and 50 is not more than 50.
reveal.say: Reduced by fifty percent, not barred. The cutoff applies only above fifty percent, and fifty is not more than fifty.

scenes.title: Three more kinds of liability
scenes.src: Restatement (2d) Torts §§519-520; IRMI glossary: strict, vicarious liability; LII Wex; hook mn_core-14

draw.text:
Employer for an
employee on the job
Generic exam definitions, not Michigan product law

beats.text: Three more kinds. Absolute is KABOOM: ultrahazardous, abnormally dangerous activities, like blasting or keeping wild animals. Being careful is no defense.
beats.say: Three more kinds. Absolute is KABOOM: ultrahazardous, abnormally dangerous activities, like blasting or keeping wild animals. Being careful is no defense.

beats.text: Strict is the toaster that shocks you: its maker pays even after using every care, without regard to fault. The classic case: a maker or seller of a defective, dangerous product.
beats.say: Strict is the toaster that shocks you: its maker pays even after using every care, without regard to fault. The classic case: a maker or seller of a defective, dangerous product.

beats.text: Vicarious is via someone else: you're liable for another's acts, like an employer for an employee acting in the scope of employment. It can also apply to partners, independent contractors and children.
beats.say: Vicarious is via someone else: you're liable for another's acts, like an employer for an employee acting in the scope of employment. It can also apply to partners, independent contractors and children.

beats.text: Absolute and strict both ignore fault, and sources often swap the words. On the exam, the situation is the tell. These are generic definitions, not Michigan product law.
beats.say: Absolute and strict both ignore fault, and sources often swap the words. On the exam, the situation is the tell. These are generic definitions, not Michigan product law.

scenes.title: Absolute, strict or vicarious?
scenes.src: Restatement (2d) Torts §§519-520; IRMI glossary; questions core-028, core-029, core-bas-09, core-bas-10

cards.text: A crew blasting with explosives takes every precaution, yet is held liable for damage to nearby buildings.
cards.why: Blasting is ultrahazardous. Using every precaution is no defense: absolute liability.

cards.text: A clerk stocking shelves carelessly drops a heavy box on a shopper. The store is held liable.
cards.why: The store is liable for its employee's act in the scope of employment: vicarious liability.

cards.text: A maker used every possible care, yet is held liable when its defective, dangerous product injures a buyer.
cards.why: Liability without regard to fault for a defective, dangerous product: strict liability.

cards.text: Someone keeps a wild animal, takes every precaution, and is still held liable when it injures a visitor.
cards.why: Keeping wild animals is a classic absolute-liability case: being careful is no defense.

cards.text: A delivery driver negligently injures a pedestrian while making deliveries. His employer is held liable.
cards.why: An employer is liable for its employee's acts in the scope of employment: vicarious liability.

cards.text: A store sells a defective toaster that shocks a buyer. The store is held liable without regard to fault.
cards.why: A seller of a defective, dangerous product, liable without regard to fault: strict. Blasting and wild animals would be absolute.

beats.text: Your turn: absolute, strict or vicarious?
beats.say: Your turn: absolute, strict or vicarious?

reveal.text: The tell: blasting and wild animals are absolute. Defective products are strict. Someone else's act is vicarious.
reveal.say: The tell: blasting and wild animals are absolute. Defective products are strict. Someone else's act is vicarious.

scenes.title: Tony's call: Joey and the barber's window
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: vicarious liability; LII Wex: vicarious liability; question core-028; memory hook mn_core-11

beats.text: Next morning, Tony's employee Joey, shoveling Tony's walk on his shift, carelessly flings a chunk of ice through the barber's window.
beats.say: Next morning, Tony's employee Joey, shoveling Tony's walk on his shift, carelessly flings a chunk of ice through the barber's window.

beats.text: Who's paying for my window?
beats.say: Who's, paying for my window?

beats.text: What does Tony say?
beats.say: What does Tony say?

options.label: He was on the job for me. I'll answer for it
options.win: Vicarious liability: an employer is liable for an employee's acts in the scope of employment, like Joey shoveling Tony's walk.

beats.text: He was doing my work. I'll make it right.
beats.say: He was doing my work. I'll make it right.

beats.text: That's vicarious liability: Tony answers for Joey's act on the job.
beats.say: That's vicarious liability: Tony answers for Joey's act on the job.

options.label: Joey threw it. Not my problem!
options.fail: Vicarious liability: an employer is liable for its employee's acts in the scope of employment. Joey was shoveling Tony's walk.

beats.text: Joey threw it, not me!
beats.say: Joey threw it, not me!

beats.text: Joey was doing his job. An employer is liable for an employee's acts in the scope of employment.
beats.say: Joey was doing his job. An employer is liable for an employee's acts in the scope of employment.

options.label: Nobody meant to break it, so nobody pays
options.fail: Intent to harm is not an element of negligence. Joey's careless throw can still make someone liable, and that includes Tony, his employer.

beats.text: Intent isn't required. A careless act that breaks a window can still make someone liable.
beats.say: Intent isn't required. A careless act that breaks a window can still make someone liable.

reveal.text: Vicarious: liable for someone else's act. Nothing was ultrahazardous, and no product was defective.
reveal.say: Vicarious: liable for someone else's act. Nothing was ultrahazardous, and no product was defective.

items: Negligence: duty, breach, proximate cause, damage. No intent needed
Michigan: fault cuts damages; over 50% loses noneconomic
Special adds up; general is pain and suffering
Michigan punitive damages need a statute
Absolute: blasting. Strict: defective product. Vicarious: via others

beats.text: To recap: negligence needs duty, breach, proximate cause and damage, not intent. In Michigan, your own fault cuts your damages; over 50% costs you noneconomic damages. Special damages add up; general is pain and suffering.
beats.say: To recap: negligence needs duty, breach, proximate cause and damage, not intent. In Michigan, your own fault cuts your damages; over fifty percent costs you noneconomic damages. Special damages add up; general is pain and suffering.

beats.text: Michigan punitive damages need a statute, the Legislature's permission. Absolute, strict and vicarious each have a classic case. Blasting is absolute, a defective product is strict, and vicarious liability comes via others.
beats.say: Michigan punitive damages need a statute, the Legislature's permission. Absolute, strict and vicarious each have a classic case. Blasting is absolute, a defective product is strict, and vicarious liability comes via others.
